summary: NIFTY 50 on NSE_INDEX, which Arrow streams by token like any instrument: an ltpc packet as LTP, then a quote packet as an index Quote frame (no trade, book or OI fields; the change worked out from the previous close).

notes: An index quote packet carries zeros for quantities, OI and the trade time; no live index packet was recorded.

deviations.reason: data.mode is the label every broker's frames carry on the desktop (ltp, quote, full), as the recorded Zerodha transcripts carry it; the Arrow web adapter sends no data.mode.

The Arrow web adapter adds the broker's instrument token as a string to every frame; the desktop's common carrier has no place for it. Whether the desktop carries it is the lead's decision (a broker identifier, not a market field).
The Arrow web adapter repeats ltp as last_price in every frame; the desktop sends no such alias yet.
The Arrow web adapter repeats the previous close as prev_close wherever it sends close; the desktop sends no such alias yet.
The web sends the change against the previous close for every instrument whose packet carries a close (ltpc, quote, full); the desktop sends it in index Quote and Depth frames only.
deviations.ref: arrow_adapter.py:209-212; audit C04 (change on all exchanges)

deviations.reason: An LTP subscription streams Arrow's ltpc packet, whose previous close the web puts in the LTP frame (with the change); the desktop's LTP frame carries ltp and the times only. For an index the web's LTP frame also carries the change.
deviations.ref: arrow_mapping.py:54-68 (LTP -> ltpc for the close); arrow_adapter.py:206-212; audit C03

deviations.reason: An index has no trades or book: the desktop's index Quote frame leaves out last_quantity, average_price and the book totals, as the recorded Zerodha index frames do; the web passes on the zeros Arrow's quote packet carries in their place.
